country: Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and other African countries (AfriMed-QA benchmark; authored by African medical professors)
models_evaluated: over 40 LLMs including smaller and biomedical models

links.outcome: LLM accuracy on specialty-specific benchmark questions, including surgery, pathology, and obstetrics
links.effect: Top models (o1, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5) exceeded 82% mean accuracy but consistently underperformed in surgery, pathology, and obstetrics compared with medical disciplines.
links.quote: Top models (o1, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5) achieved mean accuracies exceeding 82%, showing strong diagnostic reasoning, yet consistently underperformed in surgery, pathology, and obstetrics compared with medical disciplines.

links.outcome: Overconfident but incorrect answers from LLMs
links.effect: Error analyses revealed overconfident but incorrect answers, along with procedural reasoning failures and omission of local clinical guidelines.
links.quote: Error analyses revealed frequent procedural reasoning failures, omission of local clinical guidelines, and overconfident but incorrect answers.

links.outcome: Omission of local clinical guidelines and procedural reasoning failures in LLM answers
links.effect: Error analyses revealed frequent procedural reasoning failures and omission of local clinical guidelines.
links.quote: Error analyses revealed frequent procedural reasoning failures, omission of local clinical guidelines, and overconfident but incorrect answers.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates over 40 LLMs on the AfriMed-QA benchmark across specialties with safety and error analysis, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
